skills: Year 1
Circuit analysis by hand until nodal and mesh are automatic (EEE 101, then EEE 201).
A circuit simulator: build every lab circuit in it before you touch the bench.
Bench basics: multimeter, oscilloscope, function generator, breadboard, soldering.
Programming from EEE 105 used on a real problem - plotting, solving, automating a calculation.
Year 2
Electronics you can debug: diodes, BJTs, MOSFETs, op-amps (EEE 102, EEE 202).
A numerical computing tool for EEE 204: matrices, plots, simple simulations.
Digital logic from truth table to working hardware (EEE 205).
A lab report format you no longer have to think about.
Year 3
One microcontroller platform taken to a finished device (EEE 306).
Machines and power-system calculations with per-unit values (EEE 301, EEE 304).
Signals and DSP in software before the exam (EEE 303, EEE 309).
Reading datasheets and standards as a habit; a wiring and load schedule for EEE 300.
Year 4
The toolchain of your elective group: device and circuit design tools, an RF or communications toolbox, an embedded stack, or power-system and protection studies.
A design project with requirements, alternatives, a budget, test results and a safety case.
Technical writing: a report someone else could rebuild your project from.
One outside proof: an internship, an IEEE paper or poster, or a competition placing.
dept.career_intro: EEE splits early into a few very different lives - the power sector, electronics and semiconductors, telecom, embedded and automation, software, or research. Your elective group and your Final Year Design Project are the two loudest signals on your CV, so point them the same way. These are common directions, not EWU rules.
careers: Power generation, transmission and distribution
Operating, planning and protecting the grid in public utilities and private power producers.
Group D electives, machines and power systems solid, recruitment-exam practice for utility jobs.
Electronics and semiconductors
Device, circuit and chip design or testing; electronics manufacturing.
Group A electives, a circuit or VLSI design in a real tool flow, strong EEE 202 and EEE 308.
Telecommunications and RF
Network planning, optimisation and RF engineering with operators and vendors.
Group B electives, EEE 307 and EEE 309, a communications project with measured results.
Embedded systems, automation and IoT
Firmware, control and instrumentation for products and factories.
Group C electives, EEE 306 and EEE 402, a working device; PLC exposure from the control lab.
Renewable energy
Designing and commissioning solar and storage systems.
EEE 445 Renewable Energy, EEE 447 Power Electronics, a sizing study for a real site.
Building services and consultancy
Electrical design for buildings: loads, wiring, protection, lighting.
EEE 300 Electrical Services Design taken seriously; drafting skills; a complete design set.
Software and data
Many EEE graduates move into software, data or machine learning.
EEE 105 plus a second language, data structures on your own, EEE 436 Introduction to Machine Learning.
Research and higher study
A master's or PhD, then research, teaching or advanced industry roles.
CGPA, EEE 490 Research Project, a paper or poster, two recommenders who supervised your work.
career_notes: Accreditation, as the department states it

The department's page says the B.Sc. in EEE is accredited by the Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education (BAETE), the accreditation body under the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB). If you plan to apply for professional membership or study abroad, keep that statement with your transcript.

Unofficial. An independent planner for students. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or issued by East West University. Always confirm requirements with your advisor, the student portal and official notices.

book.text: This planner puts your whole EEE degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.

items: **Degree** - the B.Sc. in Electrical and Electronic Engineering as EWU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on EWU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - EWU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.
It is **not an official EWU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from EWU's own web pages on 10 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.
On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from East West University's published pages as they stood on 10 October 2026; the source is named under each section.
A+ to D are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA.

items: **An F stays in the sum.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top, until you retake the course and the old F becomes an R.
**Heavier courses move the CGPA more.** A 4-credit course with a lab outweighs a 3-credit one. Protect the heavy courses first.
**W, I, P and S never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

Use it on purpose, not by accident: the deadline falls about two weeks before classes end.
A repeated course. An earlier attempt that a retake has replaced. No credit, not in GPA, still printed on the grade report.
Pass / Satisfactory. Counts toward graduation, not in GPA.

items: You may retake a course **only once** to improve a grade you already earned.
An **F can be retaken as many times as it takes** to pass, inside the time limit for graduation. The earlier F becomes R.
Only your **most recent attempt** counts in GPA and CGPA. Every attempt stays on the grade report.
A retake needs the **Department Chair's written permission** and full tuition, lab and other fees.
Students who use the retake policy are **not eligible for the Gold Medal, awards or distinction**, and the scholarship rules list retaking courses among the things that make a student ineligible.

book.title: Before you retake a passing grade
items: Run the numbers in the CGPA tab's retake what-if. A B- to A- retake on a 3-credit course lifts 2.25 quality points - on 90 GPA credits that is 0.025 of CGPA. Decide whether that is worth a full course fee and your scholarship eligibility.

rows: CGPA from 1.00 to below 2.25 after your first two semesters, or any later one, puts you on probation for the next two semesters. Reach 2.25 by then or be dismissed. On probation you cannot drop a semester or take leave.
CGPA below 1.00 after the first two or any later semester means automatic dismissal. A dismissed student may apply to another program by passing its admission test.
The academic calendar sets an in-person advising day for students with CGPA 2.15 or less (admitted up to Summer 2023) or 2.40 or less (admitted from Fall 2023), and for everyone on probation.

A student in good standing can take up to three consecutive semesters (one academic year) of leave through the Dean, naming the return semester. Absence without permission is penalised - 20%, 30% or 40% of nine credits' tuition for one, two or three semesters - and beyond three semesters you are withdrawn.
The student rules ask for attendance of not less than 70%-80% of lectures, tutorials and practical classes in each course. Check each course outline for the figure your instructor applies.

Final scripts are not re-evaluated. You can ask for a check of marking or totalling errors for Tk 200 a script (refunded if the error was the faculty member's). Grade changes must reach the Controller of Examinations within seven days of the next semester.

Zero tolerance for copying, unauthorised help and other unfair means; cases go to the Dean. EWU also publishes a Plagiarism Policy and an Artificial Intelligence Policy (ewubd.edu/ewu-policies) - read both before you submit work made with any tool.

book.text: the Toolkit tab - The EEE toolkit
Six tools for the way EEE is actually examined: on the bench, on paper with units, in a simulator, and finally in a design you have to defend.

You take **six electives worth at least 20 credits**. Theory-only electives are 3 credits; those with a lab are 4. If you take **EEE 490 Research Project (6 credits)**, the other 14 credits come from four electives. Electives sit in four groups - you may mix, but two or three from one group makes a specialisation an employer can read.

EEE 450 Special Topic in Electrical and Electronic Engineering
8 + 12 = 20 - the minimum, so at least two of your six carry a lab

A design project is judged on the design process as much as the device, so keep evidence of every decision.

Every 4-credit EEE course has a lab mark. The students who score on it arrive knowing what the meter should read.

rows: Read the experiment sheet. Solve the circuit by hand and write down the values you expect. Simulate it if a simulator applies. Draw the connection diagram.
Check ratings and polarity before power. Record every reading with its unit and range. If a reading is far from the expected value, find out why before moving on.
Complete the data table, compute the percentage error, and write the discussion while you remember what happened.
Be able to explain each component's job, what would change if a value doubled, and the main source of error.

book.text: 4. Solve circuits on paper without losing marks
Most marks lost in EEE 101, 102, 201 and 202 are not lost to theory. They go to signs, units and unlabelled diagrams. Use the same six steps on every problem.

items: **Redraw** the circuit cleanly. Label every node, every current with a direction, every voltage with a polarity.
**Choose the method** before you write an equation: nodal, mesh, superposition, Thevenin/Norton, phasors, small-signal model.
**Write the equations** in symbols first. Substitute numbers only at the end.
**Carry units** through every line. Convert kilo, milli and micro once, at the start.
**Sanity-check**: power supplied equals power absorbed; a voltage across a short is zero; the answer has a believable size.
**Box the answer** with its unit and, for AC, its form (rms or peak, polar or rectangular).

book.text: EEE 490 Research Project is a 6-credit elective - the department's Elective Courses page asks for 90 completed credit hours and spreads it over three semesters - and a research-flavoured design project is the best preparation for graduate study. Start from what the department's faculty already work on:

items: Photovoltaic devices and systems, Semiconductor device modelling, simulation and characterisation, Silicon-based nanoelectronics, Biosensors (silicon nanowire, paper-based, non-invasive), Micro and nanofabrication, Photonics, Grid-tied PV systems, solar farms and bifacial PV, Power converters, Electric vehicle systems, Image processing, Deep-learning energy forecasting, Engineering education.

book.text: EEE splits early into a few very different lives - the power sector, electronics and semiconductors, telecom, embedded and automation, software, or research. Your elective group and your Final Year Design Project are the two loudest signals on your CV, so point them the same way. These are common directions, not EWU rules.
